label: Faith of the rite
summary: The faith that the rite belongs to.
details: Works on a rite. The game documents it as the rite's parent faith.

label: Rite founder
summary: The character who founded the rite.
details: Works on a rite.

label: Type of the rite
summary: The rite type of the rite.
details: Works on a rite. The result is a rite type, not the rite itself.

label: Rite type by key
summary: The rite type with the key you write after the colon.
details: Written `rite_type:<key>`. It works anywhere, from any starting point.

label: Root
summary: The character, title or other thing at the top of the current script block, such as the receiver of an event or the taker of a decision.
details: It always points back to where the whole script started, however deep inside nested blocks you are. It works anywhere. Vanilla uses it very often.

label: Saint's burial province
summary: The province where the saint is buried.
details: Works on a character. The game says it applies "if applicable", so it only gives a result for a character who has a burial province as a saint.

label: Saint of the province
summary: The saint who is buried in the province.
details: Works on a province.

label: Scheme of the contract
summary: The scheme that belongs to the task contract, if there is one.
details: Works on a task contract. Not every contract has a scheme, so check that one exists before relying on it.

label: Scheme artifact
summary: The artifact connected to the scheme.
details: Works on a scheme. Vanilla does not use it.

label: Scheme defender
summary: The defender of the scheme.
details: Works on a scheme.

label: Scheme owner
summary: The character who owns the scheme.
details: Works on a scheme. Vanilla uses it a lot, nearly 900 times.

label: Scheme target
summary: The character the scheme is aimed at.
details: Works on a scheme. If the scheme's target is not a character, there is nothing to point to.

label: Scheme target culture
summary: The culture the scheme is aimed at.
details: Works on a scheme. If the scheme's target is not a culture, there is nothing to point to.

label: Scheme target faith
summary: The faith the scheme is aimed at.
details: Works on a scheme. If the scheme's target is not a faith, there is nothing to point to.

label: Scheme target title
summary: The title the scheme is aimed at.
details: Works on a scheme. If the scheme's target is not a title, there is nothing to point to.

label: Saved scope
summary: A character, title or other thing that was saved earlier under a name.
details: Written `scope:<name>`, for example `scope:target`. The name must have been saved earlier, or the link gives nothing. It works anywhere.

label: Secret faith
summary: The character's secret faith.
details: Works on a character. Vanilla uses it 45 times.

label: Secret owner
summary: The character who owns the secret.
details: Works on a secret. The secret's target is a different link, `secret_target`.

label: Secret target
summary: The target character of the secret.
details: Works on a secret.

label: Side commander
summary: The commander of one side of a combat.
details: Works on a combat side.

label: Primary participant
summary: The primary participant of one side of a combat.
details: Works on a combat side. The game does not say how it differs from the commander.

label: Situation by key
summary: The situation of the type whose key you write after the colon.
details: Written `situation:<key>`. The game says it is only available if the situation type has `is_unique = yes`. It works anywhere.

label: Center of the situation
summary: The province that was set as the situation's center.
details: Only set when the script has used the `set_situation_center_province` effect before. Otherwise the result is an empty (invalid) province. Works on a situation, e.g. `scope:situation.situation_center_province.county`.

label: Participant group by name
summary: The participant group with the given name in the situation.
details: Written `situation_participant_group:<name>`. Works on a situation. The game says it takes the first group with that name, for the top sub-region.

label: Sub-region by key
summary: The sub-region of the situation with the given key.
details: Written `situation_sub_region:<key>`, for example `situation_sub_region:west_region`. Works on a situation.

label: Top barter goods holder
summary: The participant of the situation who has the most barter goods.
details: Works on a situation. Only characters taking part in the situation are compared. Vanilla does not use it.

label: Richest participant
summary: The participant of the situation who has the most gold.
details: Works on a situation. Only characters taking part in the situation are compared. Vanilla does not use it.

label: Top herd holder
summary: The participant of the situation who has the most herd.
details: Works on a situation. Only characters taking part in the situation are compared.

label: Participant group of a character
summary: The participant group of the top sub-region that a given character belongs to.
details: Works on a situation and needs data after the colon. The game's documentation speaks of a given character but does not show how it is passed, and vanilla never uses it.

label: Top provisions holder
summary: The participant of the situation who has the most provisions.
details: Works on a situation. Only characters taking part in the situation are compared. Vanilla does not use it.

label: Top sub-region
summary: The top sub-region of the situation, with its geographic, county and province information.
details: Works on a situation.

label: Slot character
summary: The character of the agent slot.
details: Works on an agent slot.

label: Special character
summary: The special character of the faction.
details: Works on a faction. The game says nothing more about what makes the character special.

label: Special guest by type
summary: The special guest of the given type in the activity.
details: Written `special_guest:<type key>`. Works on an activity. The game lists no input or output type for it; vanilla uses it very often.

label: Special title
summary: The special title of the faction.
details: Works on a faction.

label: State faith
summary: The faith that the title's state rite belongs to.
details: Works on a title. Vanilla uses it once.

label: State rite
summary: The state rite of the title.
details: Works on a title.

label: Story owner
summary: The character who owns the story.
details: Works on a story.

label: Struggle by key
summary: The struggle with the key you write after the colon.
details: Written `struggle:<key>`. It works anywhere.

label: Sub-region group by name
summary: The participant group with the given name in the situation sub-region.
details: Written `sub_region_participant_group:<name>`. Works on a situation sub-region. Vanilla does not use it.

label: Contract of the obligation level
summary: The vassal contract of the given contract obligation level.
details: Works on a vassal contract obligation level. The game's documentation says "type of a given contract obligation" and the result is a vassal contract; vanilla uses it once.

label: Religious superior
summary: The character's religious superior.
details: Works on a character. Challengers (antipopes) count as subordinates of the top superior, so be careful when you walk up the chain.

label: Suzerain
summary: The character's suzerain.
details: Works on a character.

label: Task contract
summary: The task contract connected to the scheme, if there is one.
details: Works on a scheme.

label: Contract destination
summary: The destination province of the task contract.
details: Works on a task contract. Empty when the contract does not use a destination.

label: Contract employer
summary: The employer of the task contract.
details: Works on a task contract.

label: Contract location
summary: The province that is the location of the task contract.
details: Works on a task contract.

label: Contract taker
summary: The character who has taken the contract.
details: Works on a task contract. Empty until someone takes it.

label: Contract target
summary: The target character of the task contract.
details: Works on a task contract. Empty when the contract does not use a target.

label: Contract type by key
summary: The task contract type with the key you write after the colon.
details: Written `task_contract_type:<key>`. It works anywhere. Vanilla does not use it.
